text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A senior deputy from the ruling Islamist party says the Iranian ambassador, who called for the implementation of Islamic sharia law at an anti-Israel rally, is leaving Turkey as his period of duty is about to end.
- A bodyguard of an Islamist mayor in Ankara is arrested for punching a reporter from a private television channel.
- The leader of the junior coalition partner Tansu Ciller says the two ruling parties are like one, rebuffing rumours about the government splitting up.
- Some 3,000 attend the trial of policemen charged with involvement in the killing of a leftist journalist in custody last year.
- Opposition parties trying to topple the Islamist-led government seek the transfer of MPs from the coalition to their parties.
- Fenerbahce soccer club dismisses its technical director Sebastiao Lazaroni.
- Oil producing factories face crisis in the Thrace region due to instability and a lack of raw material.
- Turkish and Greek Cypriots clash on the divided island.
